# SoK Working Scaffold: Comparative constitutional law

## Research Frame

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Field | Comparative constitutional law |
| Learner | graduate reader |
| Goal | compare interpretive methods |
| Time budget | 4 weeks |
| Provisional lens | interpretive or contested candidate |
| Why only provisional | User supplied profile proposal remains provisional until source review. |
| Profile proposal | interpretive |
| Profile proposer type | user |
| Profile locale | en |
| Profile version | 1.0.0 |
| Profile confidence | 0.72 |
| Profile rationale | User expects case comparison and schools of interpretation, but sources must confirm or revise the profile. |

## Field Element Inventory

| Element class | Observed element | Actual form in this field | Role: core / surrounding / context | Load-bearing relations | Source IDs | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Method | Case comparison | Courts compare reasoning patterns across constitutional systems. | core | Method choices shape which cases count as comparable. | Comparative Law Review | high |
| Representation | Rights analysis framework | A model organizes rights claims, limits, and proportionality tests. | surrounding | The representation clarifies but does not replace legal warrant. | Comparative Law Review | medium |
| Failure mode | Selective case sampling | A comparison considers only courts that reached the same outcome. | context | Sampling choices limit the conclusions drawn from the cases. | Comparative Law Review | medium |
